name: reduced_nitrogen_reactor
description: A reusable FeS-mediated reduced-nitrogen module. The real ReducedNitrogenProductionProcess reduces NO3-/NO2- to NH4+ on an Fe/Ni/S catalyst (H2-dependent, temperature-windowed), adds a minor abiotic N2-fixation source, and draws ammonium into amino-acid precursors by reductive amination at a rate set by the carbon-fixation demand. Tracks the C:N supply ratio (carbon demand / reduced-N production) to test whether reduced nitrogen keeps pace with reduced carbon. fes_activity=0 / h2=0 are the no-mineral / no-reductant controls.

no3_supply.description: Open-flow nitrate feed (M/s); sets the ceiling on sustained reduced-N production

fes_activity.description: Active Fe/Ni/S catalyst in [0,1] (0 = no-mineral control)

c_demand.description: Carbon-fixation demand pulling reduced N into precursors (mol/s)

n2.description: Dissolved N2 available for minor fixation (M)

loss_rate.description: Open-flow washout of NH4+/precursor (1/s); 0 = closed batch (conservation control)

nitrogen.doc:
FeS-mediated reduction of NO3-/NO2- (and minor N2 fixation) to NH4+, with
reductive amination toward amino-acid precursors at a carbon-demanded rate.

Emits pool concentration increments (additive float deltas — pools accumulate)
plus overwrite sensors for the ammonium-production rate, the C:N supply ratio,
the reduced-N mass and the per-step nitrogen-mass residual.

_contract.summary: FeS-mediated NO3-/NO2- -> NH4+ (+ minor N2 fixation) with carbon-demanded reductive amination; tracks the C:N supply ratio and conserves nitrogen mass.
_contract.description: Emits pool concentration increments (additive float deltas - pools accumulate) for H2-driven, FeS-catalysed reduction of nitrate through nitrite to ammonium, a minor abiotic N2-fixation source on fresh FeS, and reductive amination of ammonium into amino-acid precursors at a rate set by the carbon-fixation demand. Each rate is gated by reductant availability (H2), an FeS temperature window and catalyst activity (0 = no-mineral control). An open-flow nitrate feed and ammonium washout give a condition-dependent steady state, so the ammonium-production rate and the C:N supply ratio (carbon demand / reduced-N production) are sustained-throughput sensors. Nitrogen mass is conserved by construction; n_mass_residual is the accounting witness.

inputs.fes_activity: active Fe/Ni/S catalyst in [0,1] (dimensionless; 0 = no-mineral control)
inputs.c_demand: carbon-fixation demand pulling reduced N into precursors (mole/second)

outputs.total_n: total nitrogen atoms across all pools (molar, matter accounting)
outputs.n_mass_residual: per-step nitrogen-mass accounting error (molar; ~0 by construction)

assumptions: Nitrate reduction NO3- -> NO2- -> NH4+ on FeS (Est-2024-style dissimilatory route).
N2 fixation on FeS is a LOW-yield minor source (Doerr-2003 ~0.1% relative yield).
rate = k * fes_activity * avail(H2) * T-window * [substrate]; amination scales with c_demand.
Nitrogen atoms conserved internally; only the nitrate feed and ammonium washout are sources/sinks.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
